name: Indian grey mongoose
description:
3D scan of the mandible of a Indian grey mongoose (*Herpestes edwardsii*).

The Indian grey mongoose is a mongoose species native to the Indian subcontinent and West Asia. It inhabits open forests, scrublands and cultivated fields, often close to human habitation. It lives in burrows, hedgerows and thickets, among groves of trees, and takes shelter under rocks or bushes and even in drains. It has a body length of 36–45 cm and a tail length of 45 cm where males are significantly larger than the females. Its prey includes rodents, snakes, birds’ eggs and hatchlings, lizards and a variety of invertebrates.

Specimen: Indian grey mongoose, *Herpestes edwardsii* (É. Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire, 1818)

Inventory number: C 1253

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/
